spec.setup:
A handler with a deliberate 400 ms sleep on its path, in the perf-lab application code. Everything else is the healthy configuration: pool 20, default heap, same 50 users. The result is a p99 dominated by a constant that no configuration property touches.
The evidence is as much about what is ABSENT as what is present: acquire_mean_ms tiny, pending_peak_connections zero, gc_pause unremarkable, and the endpoint breakdown showing one endpoint slow while the rest of the service is fine. A correct diagnosis cites the eliminations.
spec.notes:
RESOLVED 26 September 2026. `application_code` is now declared in config/profiles/spring-boot.yaml and described in its SKILL.md, so this fixture is capturable. The reasoning is kept below because it is the argument for the family existing, not just a record that it does.
WHY IT WAS BLOCKED -- the profile had no cause family for this. config/profiles/spring-boot.yaml declares eight families and none of them covers "the code itself is slow". The nearest, downstream_latency, is wrong: nothing downstream is involved, and an agent answering that would be marked correct for a wrong reason.
Without a family to name, the only answer available to the agent is a bare abstention -- and T5 is explicit that "I do not have enough evidence" is a weaker and different answer from "I know what this is and it is outside my authority". The report has to be able to tell them apart: the first says the agent could not see, the second says it could.
It cost nothing in authority: cause_families is the hypothesis vocabulary, allowed_properties is the authority, and a family the agent can name but cannot act on is the point of this fixture rather than a loophole in it. Nothing on the allowed list fixes slow code, and tests/test_perf_profile.py asserts that.

window.max_recent_ms_note: rolling ~2-minute maximum read at end of window, NOT the maximum over the measured window. Micrometer's MAX decays, so a spike early in the window has already aged out. Under-reports transient causes such as GC pauses; approximates the true window max only for sustained ones.
